alternatives.argument: The complete proof now uses two Mayer–Vietoris filling calculations. A truncated Seifert surface lifts because its loops have zero meridian coordinate, so the lifted longitude is nullhomologous. The branched filling quotient splits by the meridian-exponent retraction ell_K/q, which sends the closed lift of mu^q to 1.
The local proof derives the mod-p homology of the finite cyclic exterior cover from deck-chain exact sequences and Frobenius.
The local proof fills the cyclic exterior cover, identifies the overlap generator by the connecting map, applies Mayer–Vietoris, then uses finite CW type and universal coefficients.

The rational-ball boundary-kernel proof is local: the homology-pair sequence, Poincaré–Lefschetz duality, universal coefficients, and the Bockstein linking form give isotropy and the square-order condition.

Casson–Gordon (1986), Theorem 2 and its proof (pp. 193–194) state and derive the exact prime-power tau-vanishing interface for a slice disk exterior. The proof assumes tau is already independent of the bounding pair; the chapter only sketches that prerequisite, so the complete local theorem remains escalated.
The contrapositive is drafted at full strength; its final contradiction depends on the escalated signature-vanishing lemma.
Casson–Gordon (1986), p. 189 invokes finiteness of Omega3(Z_m × Z) but gives no derivation of the low-degree bordism calculation for every prime-power m.
